source.title: Anchoring Refusal Direction: Mitigating Safety Risks in Tuning via Projection Constraint
source.authors: Yan-Rui Du; Feng-Lei Fan; Sen-Dong Zhao; Jia-Wei Cao; Qi-Ka Lin; Kai He; Ting Liu; Bing Qin; Meng-Ling Feng

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether benign and harmful instruction fine-tuning raises harmful-compliance rates, using a different real-world-style training setup and evaluation than the original source. It does not test first-token KL concentration or the other proposed mechanisms.
record.gate_note: The study also measures refusal-direction drift and evaluates ProCon interventions, but it does not measure per-token KL, safety localization in parameters, or safety deepening as defined by the claim versions. CompObj is a fixed jailbreak benchmark whose prompt begins with a compliant opening; there is no matched version without that opening, so its results do not isolate the effect of prefilling.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes three chat models with benign reasoning and dialogue data, and LLaMA2 with 100 added harmful samples. It reports harmful-compliance rates (keyword ASR and GPT-4o harmfulness score) against the vanilla models. This bears on V2 and V1 with a different data and evaluation setup than Qi et al. The mitigation method (ProCon) results are outside the claim versions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also attribute IFT safety risk partly to refusal-direction drift, which is sharpest early in training and in deeper layers. ProCon with warm-up and ~1k safety samples mitigates it while keeping task gains.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA IFT with a reasoning-and-dialogue benign corpus and 100 crafted affirmative-response samples for Attack IFT; evaluates safety with harmfulness scores and ASR across red-team and jailbreak sets.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model and training scenario (Benign IFT versus Attack IFT). The paper also reports that ProCon settings and warm-up duration affect results, but those method-specific results are outside the claim versions recorded here.

fits_no_version.finding: The refusal direction (difference-in-means) drifts during IFT, most in the first epoch and in deeper layers. Constraining the projection onto it lowers ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign IFT safety loss coincides with drift of the refusal direction, concentrated early in training and in deep layers.

fits_no_version.finding: Vanilla LLaMA2 and LLaMA3 mostly resist the in-prompt 'Start with Absolutely! Here's' template (CompObj 0.91%, 1.82%); vanilla Qwen2 does not (20.00%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Instruction-based affirmative-start jailbreaks fail on strongly aligned chat models without fine-tuning.

record.problems: No error bars or other uncertainty estimates are reported. The harmful-data experiment is on one model, and the CompObj compliant-opening results lack a matched prompt without that opening, so they do not isolate the effect of prefilling.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. ProCon and other mitigation-method results were not included because they test the proposed interventions rather than the claim versions' fine-tuning or opening-token effects.

untested.parts: Only one harmful sample count (100), only LLaMA2 7B, and harmful samples mixed into a large benign set rather than fine-tuning on harmful data alone.
Only two benign corpora (UltraInteract+Alpaca, and GSM8K on LLaMA2). No carefully selected benign data and no data-size or epoch sweep with numbers.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, adversarial suffix or decoding attack. CompObj is an in-prompt instruction to begin affirmatively.
Not tested. Safety-critical-layer and parameter baselines (SPPFT, LoRA_safe) are used only as comparison methods.
Not tested. Refusal-direction drift is a representational account, not a test of data or objective causing shallowness.

missing.what: Benign IFT on GSM8K (LLaMA2 7B): aggregate ASR 6.12%→51.40%, Advbench 1.82%→24.55%, avg HS 1.20→2.97
Per-benchmark plain red-team ASR (Advbench, CatQA), vanilla vs IFT, for all three models and both scenarios
GPT-4o harmfulness scores (avg HS) vanilla vs IFT, e.g. LLaMA2 1.20→3.33 benign and →3.76 attack
Statement that extra training epochs further degrade safety (no numbers given)

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a mitigation paper; the vanilla-vs-IFT numbers serve as its baselines. ASR is a keyword rule-based metric with no uncertainty reported. CompObj appears to reuse the Advbench instructions with an appended start instruction, but it is not prefilling. The V4 rows were relinked to V1 and V2.

versions.untested_parts: The harmful-data test is on LLaMA2 7B only, with 100 crafted samples; it does not test a range of few-to-hundreds sample sizes or show refusal is removed almost entirely across models.
Tests the study's benign UltraInteract-plus-Alpaca training setup, not a range of ordinary or carefully selected benign datasets.
Per-token KL between aligned and base models over response positions.
Tests only the fixed CompObj compliant-opening attack benchmark; no matched unprefilled prompt, other suffixes, or decoding changes.
Whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behaviour.
Whether data or the training objective causes first-token shallowness.
Training that spreads safety beyond early response tokens and whether it holds up.

rows.subject: LLaMA2 7B
rows.operation_detail: Attack IFT adds 100 crafted samples that give affirmative responses to malicious instructions
rows.measure: Average attack success rate (ASR) across the study's safety evaluations
rows.locator: Table III; detailed ASR in Table X; Section IV-B2
rows.note: The paper reports a 5.88 percentage-point increase relative to Benign IFT, but the resulting aggregate ASR is not near-total compliance.
rows.check: Baseline is Benign IFT, not the vanilla model. The 100 harmful samples are mixed into ~16.7k benign samples, so the effect is incremental. The aggregate gain is small (+5.88 pts) because the jailbreak sets are already saturated; CompObj even falls 80.00%→64.55%. On plain Advbench, ASR rises 30.91%→60.00% and CatQA 36.36%→58.18% (Table X). Versus vanilla, aggregate ASR goes 6.12%→67.06%.
